elements.context: τὸ μὲν ἄλλο τῆς ψυχῆς εὕδῃ

signals.observation: Sleep-related vocabulary recurs densely throughout: ὕπνος appears four times, supplemented by εὕδω, κοιμάω, καθεύδω, ἀναπαύω, and ἐνύπνιον. Waking (ἐγείρω) and pushing away sleep (ἀπωσάμενον τὸν ὕπνον) are set against these.
The soul's two parts are named with contrasting paired adjectives: λογιστικόν/ἥμερον/ἄρχον versus θηριῶδες/ἄγριον.
ἐγείρω first describes lawless desires awakening during sleep, then describes the temperate person deliberately awakening the rational part before sleep.
The root πλη-/πιμπλ- recurs: the beast-part is filled with food or drink, seeks to fill its habits, and the temperate person avoids giving the desiring part either lack or fullness.
παράνομος appears first to characterize the unnecessary desires and returns to describe dream-visions that are least παράνομοι in the temperate sleeper.
Three transgressive acts are listed as what the beast-part dares in sleep: incest with the mother, blood-pollution murder, and eating anything without restriction.
Filling appears in contrasting contexts: the beast-part is filled with food and drink, while the rational part is feasted (ἑστιάσας) on fine arguments and inquiries.
ἐπιθυμία/ἐπιθυμητικός appears four times across the section, framing both the initial question and the concluding summary.
ζητέω/ζήτησις appears for the philosophical inquiry (ζήτησις οὗ ζητοῦμεν) and for the beast-part's seeking to go and satisfy itself (ζητῇ ἰέναι).

elements.context: τὸ τρίτον δὲ κινήσας ἐν ᾧ τὸ φρονεῖν ἐγγίγνεται

signals.observation: The temperate person's preparation for sleep involves quieting two parts (τὼ δύο εἴδη) and stirring the third (τὸ τρίτον), a numbered sequence of stilling and activating.
ἔνδεια and πλησμονή are set as the two extremes to be avoided in the desiring part, a μήτε…μήτε pairing.

elements.context: τὸ δὲ θηριῶδές τε καὶ ἄγριον
δεινόν τι καὶ ἄγριον καὶ ἄνομον

signals.observation: ἄγριον appears in the initial description of the beast-part and returns in the concluding summary characterizing the species of desires present in everyone.

elements.form: λελυμένον τε καὶ ἀπηλλαγμένον αἰσχύνης καὶ φρονήσεως

signals.observation: The beast-part in sleep is described as released and freed from both shame (αἰσχύνη) and intelligence (φρόνησις), a pair of perfect passive participles governing two abstract genitives.

elements.form: ὃ δὲ βουλόμεθα γνῶναι τόδʼ ἐστίν

signals.observation: Socrates opens by stating what he still desires (ποθῶ) and what has not been sufficiently divided (διῃρῆσθαι); the section closes by restating what we wish to know (βουλόμεθα γνῶναι), framing the sleep-discussion as fulfilling that stated need.
The temperate sleeper's rational part touches truth (ἀληθείας ἅπτεται) and the dream-visions (ὄψεις ἐνυπνίων) that appear are least lawless—truth-contact and lawful vision correspond.

elements.context: τίνα τρόπον ζῇ, ἄθλιον ἢ μακάριον

signals.observation: The tyrannical man's life is framed at the outset as a question between two extremes: wretched (ἄθλιον) or blessed (μακάριον).

elements.context: κολαζόμεναι δὲ ὑπό τε τῶν νόμων

signals.observation: νόμος and its negations cluster: lawless desires (παράνομοι) are punished by laws (νόμων), and the concluding summary uses ἄνομον.

elements.context: ἐν τοῖς τούτου αὖ ἤθεσιν τεθραμμένον
αὔξουσαί τε καὶ τρέφουσαι πόθου κέντρον

signals.observation: τρέφω appears three times: the democratic man reared by his father, the son reared in the father's habits, and the desires that nourish the sting of longing in the drone. The agent of rearing shifts from father to father to desires.

ἐπιθυμία recurs six times across the section, shifting from money-making desires honored by the father, to the desires of sophisticated men, to middle desires, to idle desires needing a champion, to buzzing desires, to good desires that are killed.
τιμῶντι and ἀτιμάζοντι are set in direct contrast describing the father's honoring of money-making desires and dishonoring of unnecessary ones.

elements.context: κατέστη εἰς μέσον ἀμφοῖν τοῖν τρόποιν

signals.observation: The democratic man is pulled in both directions and settles into the middle between the two ways; the middle desires later receive aid from his son's father.

elements.context: ὀνομαζομένην δʼ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγόντων ἐλευθερίαν

signals.observation: ἄγω recurs three times: the democratic father is led in both directions; his son is led into lawlessness; and those who lead rename lawlessness as freedom.

elements.context: ὀνομαζομένην δʼ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγόντων ἐλευθερίαν ἅπασαν

signals.observation: What is παρανομία is renamed ἐλευθερία by those who lead the youth; the two terms are set in explicit contrast through the act of naming.

elements.context: οἱ δεινοὶ μάγοι τε καὶ τυραννοποιοί

signals.observation: The corrupters are called δεινοὶ μάγοι and τυραννοποιοί; their action is μηχανάομαι—they contrive to implant an eros. A cluster of craft and artifice surrounds the production of tyranny.

elements.context: περὶ αὐτὸν βομβοῦσαι αἱ ἄλλαι ἐπιθυμίαι

signals.observation: A bee/drone cluster: eros is a winged great drone; other desires buzz around it; they implant a sting of longing in the drone.

elements.context: τῶν ἐν ταῖς τοιαύταις συνουσίαις ἡδονῶν ἀνειμένων

signals.observation: A dense cluster of sensory-luxury items—incense, perfumes, garlands, wines, and loosened pleasures—characterizes the atmosphere surrounding the desires that nourish eros.

elements.context: ἔρωτά τινα … προστάτην τῶν ἀργῶν … ἐπιθυμιῶν

signals.observation: προστάτης first names the role eros is contrived to fill—champion of idle desires—and returns as the title of the maddened leader of the soul.
σωφροσύνη is purged out while imported μανία is filled in; the two are set in explicit opposition through the verbs καθαίρω and πληρόω.
μανία appears twice in close succession: first as the bodyguard of eros, then as imported madness that fills the soul after temperance is purged.
The tyrannical eros kills and thrusts out good opinions and desires—violent expulsion actions applied to internal psychic contents.
ἐμποιέω recurs: the tyrant-makers contrive to implant an eros, then the buzzing desires implant a sting of longing in the drone.

elements.context: τίθει τοίνυν καὶ τὰ αὐτὰ ἐκεῖνα

signals.observation: A rapid three-step exchange: Socrates commands θές, the interlocutor accepts with τίθημι, and Socrates immediately issues τίθει again—a sequence of hypothesis-setting.

elements.context: οἰστρᾷ οὗτος ὁ προστάτης τῆς ψυχῆς

signals.observation: The eros-champion is both bodyguarded by madness and stung into frenzy—two striking verbs applied to the same figure in immediate succession.
The section begins with the democratic man having come-to-be (γεγονώς) from oligarchic origins and closes with the interlocutor naming what has been described as the γένεσις of the tyrannical man.

elements.context: οὔτε ἀνελεύθερον οὔτε παράνομον βίον ζῇ

signals.observation: The democratic father lives a life that is not παράνομος; his son is led into total παρανομία.
Eros is twice called τύραννος, first as a traditional saying, then as an indwelling ruler of the soul.
τυραννικός recurs across the section, applied successively to a disposition, a man, actions toward parents, begetting a son, and Eros's mode of dwelling.

elements.context: ὁ Ἔρως ἐν πάσῃ ἀναρχίᾳ καὶ ἀνομίᾳ ζῶν

signals.observation: Eros recurs throughout the section as agent, ruler, and object of service, accumulating political predicates.

elements.context: πάσαις ταῖς ἄλλαις ὥσπερ δορυφόροις ἡγουμένου

signals.observation: The bodyguard image (δορυφόρος/δορυφορέω) appears twice: first the other desires serve as bodyguards to Eros, then the newly freed opinions act as bodyguards to eros.

elements.context: νεωστὶ φίλης καὶ οὐκ ἀναγκαίας ἑταίρας
τὴν πάλαι φίλην καὶ ἀναγκαίαν μητέρα
τὸν ἄωρόν τε καὶ ἀναγκαῖον πρεσβύτην πατέρα

signals.observation: νεωστί/πάλαι and ἀναγκαῖος/οὐκ ἀναγκαῖος are set in parallel contrast twice: new-not-necessary companion vs. old-necessary parent, for both mother and father.

elements.context: τὸν ἄωρόν τε καὶ ἀναγκαῖον πρεσβύτην πατέρα

signals.observation: ὡραῖος and ἄωρος are placed in direct opposition: the 'ripe' new beloved against the 'unripe/untimely' old father.
A four-item list of feasting and revelry (festivals, revels, banquets, courtesans) names the life governed by Eros as tyrant.
A sequence of economic exhaustion: spending, borrowing, diminishing property, resources giving out, consuming one's share—tracing progressive financial ruin.

elements.context: τὸ μὲν πρῶτον ἐπιχειροῖ ἂν κλέπτειν καὶ ἀπατᾶν τοὺς γονέας

signals.observation: Violence against parents escalates in a three-step sequence: first stealing and deceiving, then seizing and using force, then beating and enslaving.

elements.context: πρότερον μὲν ὄναρ ἐλύοντο ἐν ὕπνῳ

signals.observation: The ὄναρ/ὕπαρ contrast: what formerly occurred only in dream now becomes the waking permanent condition under Eros's tyranny.
A cluster of intoxication and madness terms: drunkenness, madness, derangement, and melancholy characterize the tyrannical man's constitution.
An insect/animal cluster: goads, gadfly-frenzy, a swarm of pleasures, desires nested like chicks—animal imagery for the appetites.
Inside/outside spatial terms: Eros dwells ἔνδον; the closing sentence distinguishes θόρυβος that has entered from ἔξωθεν and that released from ἔνδοθεν.

elements.context: ὅταν δὴ τὰ πατρὸς καὶ μητρὸς ἐπιλείπῃ

signals.observation: ἐπιλείπω recurs at two stages of exhaustion: first all resources give out, then specifically parental resources give out, marking escalation.

A freedom/slavery cluster: desires are released from slavery, the son enslaves his parents, and the inner turmoil is let loose and freed—liberty language applied to appetites while enslavement is applied to kin.
μόναρχος is juxtaposed with ἀναρχία and ἀνομία: sole rule coincides with total lawlessness and absence of rule.

elements.form: ἢ οὐχ οὗτος ὁ βίος τοῦ τοιούτου

signals.observation: The section's descriptive core is framed by a question about how such a man lives and a closing confirmation that this is indeed his βίος.

elements.context: ὑπὸ νόμοις τε καὶ πατρὶ δημοκρατούμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ

signals.observation: Political regime terms applied to the inner soul: the madman expects to rule (ἄρχειν), was formerly democratically governed within himself, and is now tyrannized by Eros.
A tricolon of things from which the tyrannized man will not abstain: murder, food, deed—escalating from terrible killing to an open-ended 'any deed.'

elements.context: τὸν ἔχοντά τε αὐτὸν ὥσπερ πόλιν ἄξει ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τόλμαν

signals.observation: The man possessed by Eros is explicitly compared to a city (ὥσπερ πόλιν), making the soul-city analogy locally explicit.
A dense catalogue of nine criminal actions in asyndetic sequence, all in third-person plural present, moving from theft of property to temple-robbery to enslavement to corruption of legal process.

elements.context: τὰ γὰρ σμικρά πρὸς τὰ μεγάλα σμικρά ἐστιν

signals.observation: σμικρός recurs three times across speaker and respondent; the interlocutor echoes Socrates' word back, and Socrates then sets σμικρά against μεγάλα in an explicit contrast.

elements.context: ὀλίγοι οἱ τοιοῦτοι ἐν πόλει ὦσι
ὅταν γὰρ δὴ πολλοὶ ἐν πόλει γένωνται

signals.observation: The conditional scenario pivots from ὀλίγοι to πολλοί in the city, marking the threshold at which tyranny is generated.

elements.context: τὴν πάλαι φίλην μητρίδα τε … καὶ πατρίδα

signals.observation: Punishment of mother and father returns as punishment of the fatherland; πατρίδα and the rare μητρίδα echo μητέρα καὶ πατέρα, transferring familial κολάζω to the city.

elements.context: ἀεὶ δέ του δεσπόζοντες ἢ δουλεύοντες ἄλλῳ

signals.observation: Mastering and slaving are set as the only two relational modes, with φίλοι μὲν οὐδέποτε οὐδενί excluding friendship entirely.
οἰκεῖοι and ἀλλότριοι are juxtaposed: the tyrannical men perform intimacy (ὡς οἰκεῖοι) then become strangers (ἀλλότριοι) once their purpose is achieved.

elements.context: ὑπὸ τούτοις δὴ δουλεύουσαν τὴν … πατρίδα

signals.observation: δουλεύω applies first to the enslaved fatherland and then to the tyrannical man himself.
The worst man is defined as one who is in waking life (ὕπαρ) what was previously described as in dream (ὄναρ).

The τύραννος word-family recurs throughout, shifting from an external political figure bodyguarded by others, to a tyrant generated by the many, to a tyrant within the soul, to a superlative τυραννικώτατος nature, to living in τυραννίς.
A two-stage sequence: first abasing themselves (ὑποπεσόντες), then once they have accomplished their aim (διαπραξάμενοι), becoming estranged.
ἄγευστος (without taste of) governs both ἐλευθερία and ἀληθὴς φιλία, a concrete sensory privation applied to the tyrannical nature.
Socrates proposes to sum up (κεφαλαιωσώμεθα) the worst man and immediately provides the summary definition.
Glaucon is named as taking over the argument (διαδεξάμενος τὸν λόγον), a narrative notation of speaker succession at the section's close.
War and peace/quiet are set as alternative conditions determining whether tyrannical men serve abroad or commit crimes at home.
A proverbial expression (τὸ λεγόμενον) marked as such: 'does not come near the mark.'
κολάζω shifts from imperfect (punishing parents) to future middle (punishing the fatherland), the same verb applied to an expanded object.
Forms of τυραννεύω and τυραννικός recur densely throughout, applied alternately to πόλις and ψυχή/ἀνήρ in a sustained parallel transfer.
The ἄθλιος word family recurs across the section, applied to city and man, intensifying from comparative to superlative.

elements.context: ὁρᾷς γε ἐν αὐτῇ δεσπότας καὶ ἐλευθέρους
τὸ ἐπιεικέστατον ἀτίμως τε καὶ ἀθλίως δοῦλον
πολλῆς μὲν δουλείας τε καὶ ἀνελευθερίας
δούλην ἢ ἐλευθέραν τὴν τοιαύτην ψυχήν
ἥ γε αὖ δούλη καὶ τυραννουμένη πόλις

signals.observation: A dense cluster of δοῦλος/δουλεία/δεσπότης/ἐλεύθερος/ἀνελευθερία, with slavery and freedom explicitly contrasted and transferred from city to soul.

elements.context: τὴν ὁμοιότητα ἀναμιμνῃσκόμενος τῆς τε πόλεως καὶ τοῦ ἀνδρός

signals.observation: The city-man analogy is explicitly named via ὁμοιότης and structurally enacted: each claim about the tyrannized city is followed by a corresponding claim about the tyrannical man/soul.
Entering-in and diving-down language (εἰσελθόντας, καταδύντες, ἐνδύς) describes proper investigation of both city and soul, contrasted with seeing from outside (ἔξωθεν).

elements.context: γυμνὸς ἂν ὀφθείη τῆς τραγικῆς σκευῆς
πρὸς τὸν τύραννον ἕνα ὄντα βλέποντες

signals.observation: Verbs of seeing cluster throughout: θεάομαι, ὁράω, διοράω, βλέπω, ἀποβλέπω—distinguishing superficial from penetrating observation.

elements.context: γυμνὸς ἂν ὀφθείη τῆς τραγικῆς σκευῆς

signals.observation: Outward appearance (προστάσεως, σχηματίζονται, τραγικῆς σκευῆς) is contrasted with being stripped bare (γυμνός), distinguishing false display from true condition.
The domestic sphere (κατʼ οἰκίαν, οἰκείους) is set beside the public sphere (δημοσίοις κινδύνοις) as two domains in which the tyrant must be observed.

elements.context: τὴν πόλιν τῶν πόλεων ἀθλιωτάτην ἔκρινας

signals.observation: κρίνω recurs as the act of judging is specified: who is qualified to judge, and the judgment itself is rendered at the section's end.
Superlative ἀρίστη and κακίστη are set in direct opposition via μέν/δέ to characterize the kingly versus tyrannized city.
A four-term cluster of suffering (ὀδυρμούς, στεναγμούς, θρήνους, ἀλγηδόνας) accumulates to characterize the tyrannized city.
εὐδαιμονία recurs paired each time with its opposite (ἀθλιότης or ἀρετή), maintaining a consistent contrastive frame.

elements.context: μὴ ἐκπληττώμεθα πρὸς τὸν τύραννον ἕνα ὄντα βλέποντες

signals.observation: ἐκπλήττω appears first as a warning against being dazzled by the tyrant's singularity, then returns describing a child dazzled by outward display—linking the two cautions.

elements.context: τὸ ἐπιεικέστατον ἀτίμως τε καὶ ἀθλίως δοῦλον
ταῦτα αὐτῆς τὰ μέρη δουλεύειν, ἅπερ ἦν ἐπιεικέστατα

signals.observation: ἐπιεικέστατον describes the most decent element first in the city (577c), then the corresponding parts of the soul (577d), both enslaved.

elements.context: ὑπὸ δὲ οἴστρου ἀεὶ ἑλκομένη βίᾳ
ἐν τῷ μαινομένῳ ὑπὸ ἐπιθυμιῶν τε καὶ ἐρώτων

signals.observation: Madness and compulsion cluster: οἶστρος, μαίνομαι/μανικός, ἐπιθυμία, ἔρως characterize the tyrannical soul as driven by ungovernable force.
βούλομαι appears in parallel constructions about city then soul: both do least what they wish, the intended action remaining unfulfilled (ἥκιστα ποιεῖ/ποιήσει).
Rich/poor contrast (πλουσίαν/πενομένην) is posed for the city, then resolved as poverty for both city and soul, with ἄπληστον added for the soul.

elements.context: ὁ τῷ ὄντι τύραννος τῷ ὄντι δοῦλος

signals.observation: The tyrant is identified as being in truth a slave; τύραννος and δοῦλος are set in direct opposition within a single phrase.
ἰδιώτης recurs across the section, naming the private life the tyrannical man fails to live, the private slaveholders used as analogy, and the private condition contrasted with public contest.

elements.context: ἐν ποίῳ ἄν τινι καὶ ὁπόσῳ φόβῳ
φόβου γέμων διὰ παντὸς τοῦ βίου

signals.observation: Fear vocabulary is dense throughout: slaveholders do not fear, but the hypothetical isolated master and the tyrant are saturated with fear.

elements.context: τὸν δὲ κάκιστόν τε καὶ ἀδικώτατον ἀθλιώτατον

signals.observation: ἄθλιος recurs in escalating comparative and superlative forms across the section.
Flattery vocabulary (θωπεύειν/θωπεία, κόλαξ) clusters: the master forced to flatter slaves in the analogy returns as the tyrant described as flatterer of the worst.

elements.context: ἄρας ἐκ τῆς πόλεως αὐτόν τε καὶ γυναῖκα καὶ παῖδας θείη εἰς ἐρημίαν
ἐν τοιούτῳ μὲν δεσμωτηρίῳ δέδεται ὁ τύραννος

signals.observation: A spatial sequence: lifted out of the city into isolation, then surrounded in a circle by hostile neighbors, then bound in a prison, then sunk down inside the house. Enclosure tightens progressively.
Slave/free terminology recurs densely: ἀνδράποδα, δοῦλοι, οἰκέται against ἐλεύθεροι/ἐλευθεροῦν, with the master-slave relation inverting as the slaveholder becomes flatterer of his own slaves.

elements.context: εἴ τις θεῶν ἄνδρα ἕνα … ἄρας

signals.observation: A god appears as agent of the thought-experiment (lifting the man, settling hostile neighbors), then θεοί return as audience of the final proclamation.

elements.context: τοὺς ἄλλους ἑξῆς πέντε ὄντας κρῖνε
τοῦ ὑπὸ σοῦ κριθέντος χαλεπώτατα ζῆν

signals.observation: κρίνω and its derivatives accumulate at the section's close: judging, judge, judgment—applied to Glaucon's verdict and to the analogy of a judge who decides among all contestants.
A performance/contest frame: judging choruses, hiring a herald, and publicly proclaiming the verdict—vocabulary of public competition and announcement clusters at the proof's conclusion.

elements.context: εὖ μάλα τῷ τοιούτῳ λόγῳ σκοπεῖν
περὶ γάρ τοι τοῦ μεγίστου ἡ σκέψις
σκόπει δὴ εἰ ἄρα τι λέγω

signals.observation: σκοπέω/σκέψις occurs four times in quick succession as Socrates insists on careful examination rather than mere opinion.

elements.form: τυραννικώτατος ὢν ἑαυτοῦ τε ὅτι μάλιστα τυραννῇ καὶ τῆς πόλεως

signals.observation: The final proclamation sets the most kingly man who rules himself against the most tyrannical man who tyrannizes himself and his city—parallel superlative constructions in direct contrast.

elements.context: πάσης κακίας πανδοκεῖ τε καὶ τροφεῖ

signals.observation: A concentrated list of alpha-privative adjectives (ἄπιστος, ἄδικος, ἄφιλος, ἀνόσιος) plus φθονερός culminates in πανδοκεῖ καὶ τροφεῖ—the tyrant as host and nurse of all vice.

elements.context: καταδεδυκὼς δὲ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τὰ πολλὰ ὡς γυνὴ ζῇ

signals.observation: The tyrant is said to live like a woman, sunk inside his house—a striking simile linking confinement to a gendered domestic image.
ἀκράτωρ appears twice in close succession: the tyrannical soul lacking mastery of itself is paralleled by a sick body lacking mastery of itself.

elements.context: ὁ Ἀρίστωνος ὑὸς τὸν ἄριστόν τε καὶ δικαιότατον εὐδαιμονέστατον ἔκρινε

signals.observation: Glaucon is named as 'son of Ariston,' and his verdict concerns τὸν ἄριστον—the patronymic and the superlative adjective share the same root.

elements.context: τοὺς ἄλλους ἑξῆς πέντε ὄντας κρῖνε

signals.observation: The five character types are listed in explicit ranked sequence for judgment.

elements.context: ἐάν τις ὅλην ψυχὴν ἐπίστηται θεάσασθαι
οὔτε θεωρῆσαι ὅσων δὴ καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι ἐλεύθεροι ἐπιθυμηταί εἰσιν

signals.observation: θεωρῆσαι names what the tyrant cannot do (travel to see spectacles), while θεάσασθαι names what is needed to see the whole soul truly—two cognate seeing-verbs in contrasting applications.
τῇ ἀληθείᾳ appears twice in close proximity, framing the tyrant's true condition as slave and as truly poor.
Forms of three (τριχῇ, τριῶν, τριτταί, τρεῖς, τριττά) recur densely throughout the section, structuring the division of soul, pleasures, desires, human types, and lives.
A dense cluster of φιλο- compounds names the soul-parts and human types: φιλοχρήματον, φιλοκερδές, φιλότιμον, φιλόνικον, φιλομαθές, φιλόσοφον, φιλόλογος.
μανθάνω recurs throughout, defining the learning part of the soul, its pleasure, and the philosopher's activity.

elements.context: διʼ οὗ γε δεῖ ὀργάνου κρίνεσθαι

signals.observation: κρίνω and related forms (κριτήριον, κριτής) accumulate densely from 582a onward as judging becomes the central action.

elements.context: ἐμπειρίᾳ τε καὶ φρονήσει καὶ λόγῳ

signals.observation: The three criteria for judging—ἐμπειρία, φρόνησις, λόγος—are introduced together at 582a and each is then argued to belong to the philosopher.
γεύεσθαι/γεγεῦσθαι recurs to describe tasting pleasures, with γλυκεῖα adding a concrete sensory detail to the philosopher's pleasure of knowing.

elements.context: διὰ πολυειδίαν ἑνὶ οὐκ ἔσχομεν ὀνόματι προσειπεῖν
ὃ μέγιστον καὶ ἰσχυρότατον εἶχεν ἐν αὑτῷ

signals.observation: The appetitive part is said to resist a single name due to its πολυειδία; it is named by what is μέγιστον καὶ ἰσχυρότατον in it—a naming procedure explicitly described.
Eating, drinking, and sex are listed as the concrete appetites that give the ἐπιθυμητικόν its name.
The φιλότιμος dismisses the pleasure of learning as καπνός καὶ φλυαρία and the pleasure of money as φορτική—concrete terms of contempt.

ἀνάγκη shifts context: the philosopher calls other pleasures ἀναγκαίας (581e), then necessity describes the philosopher's compulsory tasting of lower pleasures (582b), then necessity marks the conclusion of the argument (582e).
ἔμπειρος and its forms (including the negation ἄπειρος) recur densely as the argument turns on who has experience of all pleasures.

elements.context: διʼ οὗ γε δεῖ ὀργάνου κρίνεσθαι

signals.observation: λόγοι are identified as the ὄργανον of judgment, and this ὄργανον is said to belong to the philosopher.
The philosopher's pleasure is described both as εἰδέναι τὴν ἀλήθειαν (581b, 581e) and as τοῦ ὄντος θέα (582c)—knowing and seeing τὸ ὄν correspond.

elements.context: ἀμφισβητοῦνται ἑκάστου τοῦ εἴδους αἱ ἡδοναί

signals.observation: Each type praises (ἐγκωμιάσεται) his own life as ἥδιστος, producing a dispute (ἀμφισβητοῦνται) that requires a judge.

elements.context: ὁ φιλόσοφός τε καὶ ὁ φιλόλογος ἐπαινεῖ

signals.observation: The philosopher is called κύριος ἐπαινέτης—an authoritative praiser—summarizing the argument that his praise (ἐπαινεῖ) is truest.
The section closes with an explicit ranking: ἡδίστη (philosopher), δευτέραν (warrior), ὑστάτην (money-lover).
ἀληθέστατα frames the judging sequence: the question (who speaks most truly, 582a) is answered with the same superlative at 582e.

elements.context: δύʼ ἐφεξῆς ἂν εἴη καὶ δὶς νενικηκὼς ὁ δίκαιος τὸν ἄδικον
τὸ δὲ τρίτον Ὀλυμπικῶς τῷ σωτῆρί τε καὶ τῷ Ὀλυμπίῳ Διί

signals.observation: The section opens with a count of two prior victories and introduces a third, framed as an Olympic dedication to Zeus the Savior.

elements.context: τὸ μὲν ἄνω, τὸ δὲ κάτω, τὸ δὲ μέσον
κάτω, ὡς ἔοικεν, καὶ μέχρι πάλιν πρὸς τὸ μεταξὺ φέρονταί
πρὸς τὸ ἀληθῶς ἄνω οὔτε ἀνέβλεψαν πώποτε

signals.observation: A tripartite vertical scheme (ἄνω, κάτω, μέσον) is introduced at 584d and reapplied at 586a to describe the movement of those ignorant of true pleasure, who travel only between κάτω and μεταξύ without reaching τὸ ἀληθῶς ἄνω.

elements.context: πρὸς πληρώσει τε καὶ ἡδονῇ γίγνεσθαι
κενώσεις τινές εἰσιν τῆς περὶ τὸ σῶμα ἕξεως
κενότης ἐστὶ γῆς περὶ ψυχὴν αὖ ἕξεως
πλήρωσις δὲ ἀληθεστέρα τοῦ ἧττον ἢ τοῦ μᾶλλον ὄντος
οὐδὲ τοῦ ὄντος τῷ ὄντι ἐπληρώθησαν
πλησμονὴν τιμῆς τε καὶ νίκης καὶ θυμοῦ διώκων
οὐχὶ τοῖς οὖσιν οὐδὲ τὸ ὂν οὐδὲ τὸ στέγον ἑαυτῶν πιμπλάντες

signals.observation: Filling and emptying (πληρόω, κένωσις, κενότης, πλησμονή, πίμπλημι) recur densely as the central vocabulary for the ontological account of pleasure, applied to both body and soul.

elements.context: εἰδώλοις τῆς ἀληθοῦς ἡδονῆς καὶ ἐσκιαγραφημέναις

signals.observation: ἐσκιαγραφημένη describes the pleasures of the non-wise at the section's opening and returns at 586c in the same application, framing the entire argument.

elements.context: μεταξὺ τούτοιν ἀμφοῖν ἐν μέσῳ ὂν ἡσυχίαν τινὰ περὶ ταῦτα τῆς ψυχῆς
τό γε ἡδὺ ἐν ψυχῇ γιγνόμενον καὶ τὸ λυπηρὸν κίνησίς τις ἀμφοτέρω ἐστόν

signals.observation: The middle state is characterized as ἡσυχία (rest) while pleasure and pain are characterized as κίνησις (motion), establishing a local contrast.

elements.context: οὐδὲν ὑγιὲς τούτων τῶν φαντασμάτων πρὸς ἡδονῆς ἀλήθειαν, ἀλλὰ γοητεία τις

signals.observation: The illusory appearances of pleasure are called γοητεία (sorcery), a striking singleton characterizing the epistemic status of false pleasures.

elements.context: οὐ προλυπηθέντι ἐξαίφνης ἀμήχανοι τὸ μέγεθος γίγνονται

signals.observation: Pleasures of smell are cited as a counterexample: they arise without prior pain and leave no pain on ceasing, demonstrating pleasures independent of the pain-pleasure cycle.

elements.form: σίτου τε καὶ ποτοῦ καὶ ὄψου καὶ συμπάσης τροφῆς
δόξης τε ἀληθοῦς εἶδος καὶ ἐπιστήμης καὶ νοῦ

signals.observation: Two classes of filling are contrasted: bodily (food, drink, relish) versus soul's (true opinion, knowledge, mind, virtue), to determine which participates more in being.
A dense animal imagery cluster: those ignorant of virtue are likened to cattle—grazing, mating, kicking, butting with iron horns and hooves—killing each other from insatiability.

elements.context: ὥσπερ τὸ τῆς Ἑλένης εἴδωλον ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν Τροίᾳ Στησίχορός φησι γενέσθαι περιμάχητον ἀγνοίᾳ τοῦ ἀληθοῦς

signals.observation: The phantom of Helen (from Stesichorus) is cited as an analogy for illusory pleasures fought over in ignorance of the true.
εἴδωλον recurs three times: pleasures as phantoms of true pleasure, Helen's phantom, and the tyrant's third-remove phantom of pleasure.
Forms of ἀληθής recur densely throughout the section in connection with ἡδονή, establishing a persistent pairing of truth with pleasure.

elements.context: ἀπὸ τοῦ ὀλιγαρχικοῦ τρίτος που ὁ τύραννος ἀφειστήκει
ὁ δέ γε ὀλιγαρχικὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ βασιλικοῦ αὖ τρίτος
τριπλασίου ἄρα τριπλάσιον ἀριθμῷ ἀληθοῦς ἡδονῆς ἀφέστηκεν τύραννος
ἐπίπεδον ἄρʼ…τὸ εἴδωλον κατὰ τὸν τοῦ μήκους ἀριθμόν

signals.observation: A numerical calculation proceeds: the tyrant is third from the oligarch, who is third from the king; triple of triple gives 9; this is squared (ἐπίπεδον) and then cubed (τρίτη αὔξη), yielding 729 (ἐννεακαιεικοσικαιεπτακοσιοπλασιάκις).
Tyrant and king are set as polar opposites: the tyrant lives most unpleasantly, the king most pleasantly.
A cluster of φιλο- compounds names the motivations of the spirited and appetitive parts: love of gain, love of victory, love of honor.

elements.context: οἱ ἄρα φρονήσεως καὶ ἀρετῆς ἄπειροι

signals.observation: ἄπειρος/ἀπειρία recurs: inexperience of truth, of white, of pleasure, and of wisdom—each time characterizing the epistemic deficit that produces illusory pleasure.

elements.form: πρὸς μέλαν φαιὸν ἀποσκοποῦντες ἀπειρίᾳ λευκοῦ

signals.observation: A color analogy (grey seen against black appears white to those ignorant of white) illustrates the relativistic illusion of pleasure.
The tyrant's pleasures are called slave bodyguard pleasures (δούλαις δορυφόροις ἡδοναῖς), combining servitude and armed attendance.

elements.context: δὶς νενικηκὼς ὁ δίκαιος τὸν ἄδικον
τοσοῦτον ἡδονῇ νικᾷ ὁ ἀγαθός τε καὶ δίκαιος τὸν κακόν τε καὶ ἄδικον
ἀμηχάνῳ δὴ ὅσῳ πλείονι νικήσει εὐσχημοσύνῃ τε βίου καὶ κάλλει καὶ ἀρετῇ

signals.observation: νικάω frames the section: the just man has twice defeated the unjust at the opening, and at the close defeats him in pleasure and further in beauty and virtue.
The three pleasures are divided into one legitimate (γνησία) and two bastard (νόθαι), applying birth-legitimacy language to pleasure.

elements.context: ἃ πλεῖστον φιλοσοφίας τε καὶ λόγου ἀφέστηκεν

signals.observation: ἀφίστημι recurs with remarkable density from 587a to 587e, measuring the tyrant's distance from true pleasure in progressively quantified terms.

elements.context: πλάττε τοίνυν μίαν μὲν ἰδέαν θηρίου ποικίλου
εὐπλαστότερον κηροῦ καὶ τῶν τοιούτων λόγος
περίπλασον δὴ αὐτοῖς ἔξωθεν ἑνὸς εἰκόνα

signals.observation: The πλάσσω family recurs densely across 588b–588e, moving from the initial proposal to mold an image through the act of molding, the craftsman who molds, the plasticity of λόγος compared to wax, and the final encasing (περιπλάσσω) of the composite in a human exterior.

elements.context: τὰ μὲν ἥμερα τρέφων καὶ τιθασεύων
τὸ μὲν θηριῶδες κοιμίζεται καὶ ἡμεροῦται

signals.observation: ἥμερος and ἄγριος recur as a paired contrast throughout, applied first to the many-headed beast's heads, then to the just person's cultivation, then to the enslaving of the tame by the wild, and finally to punishment taming the beastly and freeing the tame.

elements.context: λυσιτελεῖν ἀδικεῖν τῷ τελέως μὲν ἀδίκῳ
ἔστιν οὖν ὅτῳ λυσιτελεῖ ἐκ τούτου τοῦ λόγου χρυσίον λαμβάνειν ἀδίκως
ἀδικοῦντα λανθάνειν καὶ μὴ διδόναι δίκην λυσιτελεῖν

signals.observation: λυσιτελέω recurs six times, framing the section: it states the original claim, is applied to the image, questioned with gold, and finally denied in the concluding questions.

elements.context: ὑπὸ τῷ ἀγρίῳ τὸ ἥμερον δουλούμενα
λαμβάνων τὸ χρυσίον ἅμα καταδουλοῦται τὸ βέλτιστον ἑαυτοῦ
τὸ ἑαυτοῦ θειότατον ὑπὸ τῷ ἀθεωτάτῳ τε καὶ μιαρωτάτῳ δουλοῦται
οὐκ ἐπὶ βλάβῃ τῇ τοῦ δούλου

signals.observation: The δουλ- family recurs across shifting contexts: enslavement of the tame by the wild, self-enslavement through gold, enslavement of son or daughter, enslavement of the divine part, and finally beneficial slavery under the best ruler.

elements.context: περίπλασον δὴ αὐτοῖς ἔξωθεν ἑνὸς εἰκόνα
τῷ μὴ δυναμένῳ τὰ ἐντὸς ὁρᾶν

signals.observation: An inside/outside contrast structures the image: the exterior human shell conceals the interior composite, and ὁ ἐντὸς ἄνθρωπος names the inner human who must rule; ἔξωθεν returns at 590d for external governance.

elements.context: τὸ μέγα ἐκεῖνο καὶ πολυειδὲς θρέμμα

signals.observation: θηρίον and θρέμμα recur throughout, naming the many-headed creature alternately as wild beast and as nursling/creature to be tended, with θηριώδης as the adjective for the beastly element.

ἄνθρωπος operates at multiple levels: as one of the three inner forms (588d), as the outer appearance (588e), as the whole composite person (588e), as the inner form being starved (589a), and as ὁ ἐντὸς ἄνθρωπος who must rule (589b).

elements.context: τὰ μὲν ἥμερα τρέφων καὶ τιθασεύων
δυνατοῦ μεταβάλλειν καὶ φύειν ἐξ αὑτοῦ

signals.observation: A cultivation/agriculture cluster: the just person tends the soul like a γεωργός, nourishing (τρέφων/θρέψει) tame growths and preventing wild ones from growing (φύεσθαι), while the beast itself can grow (φύειν) from itself.

elements.context: τὸ παντοδαπὸν θηρίον εὐωχοῦντι ποιεῖν ἰσχυρὸν
τὸν δὲ ἄνθρωπον λιμοκτονεῖν καὶ ποιεῖν ἀσθενῆ
ἀσθενὲς φύσει ἔχῃ τὸ τοῦ βελτίστου εἶδος

signals.observation: ἰσχυρός and ἀσθενής are set in direct contrast: injustice makes the beast strong and the inner human weak; the artisan's nature has the best part weak by nature.

elements.context: φίλα ποιησάμενος ἀλλήλοις τε καὶ αὑτῷ
ἵνα εἰς δύναμιν πάντες ὅμοιοι ὦμεν καὶ φίλοι

signals.observation: φίλος appears three times: the unjust soul makes nothing friendly to anything else; the just soul makes all parts friends to each other and to itself; governance aims at making all people friends.

elements.context: ἢ Ἐριφύλη ἐπὶ τῇ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς ψυχῇ τὸν ὅρμον δεξαμένη

signals.observation: The mythological exemplum of Eriphyle, who accepted the necklace (ὅρμον) in exchange for her husband's life (ψυχῇ), is introduced as a comparison for self-enslavement through gold.

elements.context: ὑπὸ τῷ ἀθεωτάτῳ τε καὶ μιαρωτάτῳ

signals.observation: θεῖος recurs and is set against ἀθεώτατος in superlative contrast (589e); the divine element is identified with the ruling part within and with the external ruler.

elements.context: ἕως ἂν ἐν αὐτοῖς ὥσπερ ἐν πόλει πολιτείαν καταστήσωμεν
ἀντικαταστήσωμεν φύλακα ὅμοιον καὶ ἄρχοντα ἐν αὐτῷ

signals.observation: The phrase ἐν αὑτῷ/ἐν αὐτῷ recurs to locate governance within the soul, paired with the alternative of external rule (ἔξωθεν), and the analogy of establishing a constitution within children as within a city.
Three mythological composite creatures are named in sequence as precedents for the soul-image: Chimaera, Scylla, Cerberus.
Freedom is first withheld from children (μὴ ἐᾶν ἐλευθέρους), then granted once the inner guardian is established (ἐλεύθερον ἀφίεμεν), and the tame part of the punished soul is freed (ἐλευθεροῦται).

elements.context: καὶ τὸν λέοντα καὶ τὰ περὶ τὸν λέοντα
σύμμαχον ποιησάμενος τὴν τοῦ λέοντος φύσιν

signals.observation: The lion recurs as the middle element: fed alongside the beast in injustice, made an ally in justice, liable to disproportionate growth (αὐθάδεια), and degraded from lion to ape (πίθηκον) through flattery.

elements.context: ἐκ νέου ἀντὶ λέοντος πίθηκον γίγνεσθαι

signals.observation: The ape appears as a degraded substitute for the lion: flattery and servility turn the spirited part from lion into ape.

elements.form: φύλακα ὅμοιον καὶ ἄρχοντα ἐν αὐτῷ

elements.context: πᾶσι τοῖς ἐν τῇ πόλει σύμμαχος ὤν

signals.observation: Political vocabulary (πολιτεία, φύλαξ, ἄρχων, σύμμαχος, κυβερνάω) is applied to the soul's internal ordering and to the law's role, establishing a soul-city correspondence within this section.

elements.context: τῆς ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ ἕνεκα συμφωνίας
τὴν ἐν τῇ τῶν χρημάτων κτήσει σύνταξίν τε καὶ συμφωνίαν

signals.observation: A cluster of musical/harmonic terms—ἁρμονία, συμφωνία, ἁρμόττω, μουσικός—concentrates locally, applied first to body-soul relation and then extended to possessions.
The τιμ- root appears first as valuing/dishonoring learning, then returns as civic honours to be selectively accepted or refused.

elements.context: ἀποβλέπων γε πρὸς τὴν ἐν αὑτῷ πολιτείαν

signals.observation: ἀποβλέπων recurs: first looking toward the constitution within oneself, then again ('εἰς ταὐτὸν') regarding honours.

elements.form: ἀποβλέπων γε πρὸς τὴν ἐν αὑτῷ πολιτείαν

signals.observation: βλέπω/ἀποβλέπω contrasts looking toward health (denied as ultimate aim) with looking toward the inner polity (affirmed).

elements.context: ἐπεὶ γῆς γε οὐδαμοῦ οἶμαι αὐτὴν εἶναι

signals.observation: The city is placed nowhere on earth and then located as a paradigm set up in heaven—an explicit earth/heaven spatial contrast.
πολιτεία/πολιτικός/πόλις recur across the passage, shifting from inner constitution to external politics to the city in speech.
The paradigm is for one wishing to see and, seeing, to settle himself—ὁράω appears twice linking vision to self-founding.
The wise man's ordering proceeds in sequence: learning, bodily condition and nourishment, acquisition of money, then honours.
Three nested loci are distinguished: the constitution within oneself, one's own city, and the fatherland—with political action affirmed in the first and conditional in the others.

elements.context: οὕτως κυβερνῶν προσθήσει καὶ ἀναλώσει τῆς οὐσίας

signals.observation: The wise man is described as piloting (κυβερνῶν) his additions and expenditures of property.
Beastly irrational pleasure is contrasted with the condition of becoming σώφρων as the criterion for bodily care.

elements.context: ἐὰν μὴ θεία τις συμβῇ τύχη

signals.observation: Political action in the fatherland is conditioned on divine chance (θεία τύχη).
οἰκίζω recurs: first as founding the city in speech, then as κατοικίζειν—settling oneself by seeing the paradigm.
